newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: German first division
matches this weekend (league positions in brackets):
Friday (1800GMT kickoffs)
Freiburg (18) v Borussia Moenchengladbach (10)
Moenchengladbach may be deprived of captain Stefan
Effenberg, who wants to stay with his wife who is about to give
birth.
1860 Munich (12) v St Pauli (16)
After two defeats, Munich 1860 hoping for good performance
from only injury-free striker Bernhard Winkler. St Pauli may
struggle with two players suspended and four injured.
Saturday (all 1330GMT)
Borussia Dortmund (5) v Duisburg (15)
Champions under pressure to improve poor position. Despite
promoted Duisburg's low ranking, game will be crucial test for
Dortmund, now six points behind leaders Stuttgart.
Hamburg (11) v Arminia Bielefeld (17)
Promoted Bielefeld have dismal record against Hamburg but
home side have been inconsistent this season, having failed to
win their last three games.
Werder Bremen (8) v Schalke (13)
Schalke inflicted Bremen's last home defeat -- 2-1 in May
last season. First game for Schalke's new coach Huub Stevens.
Karlsruhe (4) v Bayer Leverkusen (2)
Defender Dirk Schuster returns for Karlsruhe after
four-week suspension. Bundesliga's leading scorer, South
Africa's Sean Dundee, hoping to add to his tally as he awaits
outcome of his application for German citizenship.
Hansa Rostock (14) v VfB Stuttgart (1)
Stuttgart unbeaten away from home while Rostock finding top
division much tougher than last season. Hosts hoping striker
Jonathon Akpoborie can recover his early-season form after going
three games without a goal.
Cologne (6) v Bayern Munich (3)
Bayern, beset by injuries and rumours that international
defender Christian Ziege is considering leaving, face tough test
in Cologne, where trainer Peter Neururer has full strength
line-up.
Fortuna Duesseldorf (9) v Bochum (7)
Promoted Bochum, fresh from victory over champions Dortmund
last week, face improving Duesseldorf without their key defender
Torsten Kracht.
